planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost; Rocco is a compact pompon dahlia with tightly curled, perfectly globular flowers.

directions: Rocco is a true pompon dahlia whose silky florets curl tightly inward to form a near-perfect 2-inch sphere in a vibrant fuchsia-purple that deepens as the bloom matures, often with a slightly darker mauve center. Its sturdy, purple-flushed stems hold the small flowers upright even in windy gardens, making it reliable both in borders and in a cutting bed. The compact habit, among the shortest in the pompon class, suits small-space plantings, patio containers, and wedding or posy work. Deadhead regularly to keep the long July-to-frost bloom cycle going, and lift and store tubers after foliage blackens in zones colder than 8.

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost; Bowen is a tall-growing pompon dahlia introduced by Norman Williams in 1966, pinch young plants to encourage branching.

directions: Bowen forms small, perfectly round pompon blooms up to 2 inches across in a dainty ivory white with a soft pink blush at the center, with late-season flowers often developing fine burgundy flecks as nights cool. It is an unusually tall plant for the pompon class, carried on strong stems that hold the blooms well above the foliage for easy cutting. An early and prolific bloomer, it rewards consistent deadheading with a long season of small, uniform flowers suited to posies and mixed arrangements. Lift and store tubers after frost blackens the foliage in zones colder than 8.

common_name: Ms Kennedy Dahlia (Orange Miniature Ball Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost; Ms Kennedy is a tall miniature ball dahlia registered in 2006 by Steve and Sandy Boley, stake plants well before flowering.

directions: Ms Kennedy produces small, densely packed miniature ball flowers 2 to 3.5 inches across in a deep, glowing orange that darkens slightly toward the center. Plants grow tall for the ball class, on long, strong stems that make it a favorite among cut-flower growers for both volume and weather resistance. The tightly spiraled florets hold their shape well in the vase, and the color intensifies in cooler fall conditions. Lift and store tubers after frost blackens the foliage in zones colder than 8.

common_name: Chilson's Pride Dahlia (Pink and Cream Informal Decorative Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost; Chilson's Pride is a 1954 heirloom informal decorative that named the American Dahlia Society's 2019 Cream of the Crop list.

directions: Chilson's Pride bears small (4-6 inch) informal decorative blooms of soft pink shading to a creamy white center, with lightly ruffled petal edges giving the flower a full, fluffy texture. Introduced in 1954, it has remained a nursery staple for seventy years on the strength of its reliable performance and classic show form. Plants branch freely and produce abundant, long-stemmed blooms well suited to cutting. Stake plants at planting time, deadhead regularly, and lift and store tubers after frost blackens the foliage in zones colder than 8.

common_name: Blue Bayou Dahlia (Lilac and Purple Anemone Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost; Blue Bayou is a European-registered anemone-flowered dahlia with a spreading, free-flowering habit.

directions: Blue Bayou, sometimes sold as 'Bayou,' carries 4-inch anemone-form flowers whose flattened outer petals open in a cool mauve-lilac that frames a dense, double pincushion of deep purple tubular florets at the center. The two-tone contrast between the pale outer ring and dark inner cushion gives the bloom unusual depth for an anemone type. It flowers continuously from midsummer through fall on a spreading plant, attracting pollinators and performing equally well in borders, patio pots, and cutting gardens. Lift and store tubers after frost blackens the foliage in zones colder than 8.

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost; Lifestyle, also listed as 'Life Style,' is an RHS-recognized anemone-flowered dahlia.

directions: Lifestyle is an anemone-flowered dahlia, sometimes called a 'powder puff' type, with flamingo-pink outer ray petals surrounding a dense, feathered cushion of golden-apricot tubular florets at the center. The 3 to 4.5-inch blooms appear continuously from midsummer until frost on a compact, well-branched plant. Its refined bicolor effect and sturdy stems make it popular for both garden borders and cut-flower arrangements. Deadhead regularly, and lift and store tubers after frost blackens the foliage in zones colder than 8.

common_name: The Phantom Dahlia (Deep Pink and Orange Anemone Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after last frost; The Phantom is an anemone-flowered dahlia widely sold through European and UK bulb retailers.

directions: The Phantom opens broad, deep pink outer ray petals that gently frame a densely ruffled center where warm tones of orange, red, and pink gather in a glowing, layered cushion, giving the 3-inch flowers unusual depth and heat for an anemone type. It blooms prolifically from midsummer until frost on upright, well-branched plants. The striking color contrast and compact flower size make it a favorite for mixed borders, containers, and cut arrangements. Lift and store tubers after frost blackens the foliage in zones colder than 8.
